extraction.name: Visual Question Answering: Datasets, Algorithms, and Future Challenges
extraction.description: A review paper on visual question answering that critically examines existing datasets, evaluation metrics, algorithms, dataset biases, limitations, and future directions for VQA research.
extraction.creator: Kushal Kafle and Christopher Kanan
extraction.citeAs: Kafle, K. and Kanan, C. Visual Question Answering: Datasets, Algorithms, and Future Challenges. arXiv:1610.01465v4, 2017.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The paper reviews how several VQA datasets were collected, including DAQUAR from NYU-DepthV2 images, COCO-QA from COCO captions using an NLP algorithm, COCO-VQA from Amazon Mechanical Turk workers who generated questions and answers, FM-IQA with human-generated questions and answers, Visual Genome with free-form and region-specific question collection, and Visual7W as a subset of Visual Genome.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Manual Human Curator, Software Collection, Web Scraping, Experiments
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: The paper explicitly discusses missing or incomplete consensus in annotations, such as disagreement among annotators and questions with multiple valid answers; it also notes that some test answers for COCO-VQA were not publicly available.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Images from NYU-DepthV2, Microsoft COCO, Flickr100M/YFCC100M, synthetic cartoon scenes, and COCO captions were used as raw sources for the reviewed datasets.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: Beginning in 2014 for the major VQA datasets discussed; the review itself cites datasets and work up to 2017.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: For COCO-QA, QA pairs were derived from COCO image captions using an NLP algorithm. For COCO-VQA, questions and answers were collected via AMT. For Visual Genome, free-form and region-specific question prompting was used, leveraging bounding-box annotations. For FM-IQA, the dataset was originally collected in Chinese and English translations were made available.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: DAQUAR was provided in a smaller DAQUAR-37 configuration. COCO-QA questions were generated by breaking longer sentences into smaller chunks. COCO-VQA used consensus-based evaluation with ten answers per question. Visual Genome used descriptive bounding-box annotations to enable region-specific prompting.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: COCO-VQA used Amazon Mechanical Turk workers to generate questions and a separate pool of workers to generate answers, with ten independent annotators per question. Visual Genome used free-form questions and region-specific prompting. Visual7W used plausible answers collected by prompting annotators without seeing the image for multiple-choice options. DAQUAR-consensus collected additional ground-truth answers. FM-IQA contained human-generated questions and answers.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: The paper discusses consensus-based evaluation for COCO-VQA using ten answers per question and a scoring rule based on agreement with annotators. It also discusses DAQUAR-consensus average and min consensus, and notes annotator disagreement, subjective questions, and cases where multiple opposing answers were accepted.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: COCO-VQA: 10 answers per question; SYNTH-VQA: 10 ground truth answers per question; DAQUAR-consensus: average of 5 human annotated ground truth answers per question; Visual Genome: average of 17 QA pairs per image.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: An NLP algorithm was used to derive COCO-QA questions from captions; COCO-VQA and Visual Genome also used automated components such as bounding-box annotations and object classification during dataset construction and evaluation support.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: The paper mentions that SYNTH-VQA human cartoon models span different age, gender, and races to provide variation in appearance.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The paper states that VQA could aid blind and visually impaired individuals, improve human-computer interaction, and support image retrieval and image understanding research.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The paper repeatedly discusses language bias, answer bias, dataset imbalance, and question phrasing bias in VQA datasets. It notes that many questions can be answered without the image, that yes/no answers are heavily skewed toward 'yes' in COCO-VQA, and that free-form question collection can promote similar holistic questions.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The paper notes that many datasets are too small, contain cluttered or low-resolution images, have grammatical errors or unintelligible questions, include subjective or ambiguous questions, have poor inter-human agreement, and are limited by strong biases. It also states that multiple-choice evaluation can be gamed and that open-ended multi-word answers are difficult to evaluate automatically.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The datasets are intended for training and evaluating VQA systems; the paper also discusses validation, testing, and benchmarking. It notes that some datasets are used in open-ended or multiple-choice formats.
